newsitem.title: INDIA: India's bookies say Moopanar is odds-on favourite.
newsitem.headline: India's bookies say Moopanar is odds-on favourite.

text.p: Regional leader G.K. Moopanar will lead the next Indian government but his coalition will not last its full term -- that's the betting on New Delhi's streets, anyway.

At 1:4 odds, Moopanar, who defected from the Congress party last year to form a party in southern Tamil Nadu, was the favourite to succeed Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, according to bookies quoted in the Indian Express newspaper on Thursday.
Deve Gowda resigned last Friday after losing a parliamentary vote of confidence by a lopsided margin.
Close behind Moopanar were Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral at 1:6 and Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav at 1:10.

Farther back in the pack were communist leader Jyoti Basu at 1:20, Bihar state chief minister Laloo Prasad Yadav at 1:70, Congress president Sitaram Kesri at 1:90 and Bharatiya Janata Party leader Atal Bihari Vajpayee at 1:100.
"Most people have staked their money on the fact there would be mid-term polls, but not immediately," the daily quoted a well-heeled bookie as saying between calls on his mobile phone.
The betting is illegal but the bookies do not care.
"There is nothing on paper," the bookie said. "So the chance of our being caught is very low. I will bet 1:2 on that."
